/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 28 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2664 (-32)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4140 (-60)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1988 (-11)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1648 (-22)
Baltic Handysize Index: 900 (-3)
CAPESIZE
The market extended its retreat on Tuesday, with sentiment softening further across both the Atlantic and Pacific basins. Owners gradually lowered offers through the day, influenced in part by easing oil prices, while charterers adopted a more patient approach amid the weaker tone. The BCI 182 5TC index fell by $539 to close at $37,551. The C5 index declined by $0.455 to $12.170, while C3 lost $0.580 to settle at $33.780. In the Pacific, activity remained relatively limited, although two major miners were active alongside a reasonable volume of operator demand on C5. Despite this, the balance of power shifted in charterers’ favour as the day progressed. Opening bids around $11.75 were initially met by offers in the upper $12s, but owners quickly softened their ideas, with fixtures reported at $12.25 followed by $12.15. By the close, operators were understood to be bidding around $12.00 against owner expectations in the mid-$12s. The Atlantic also lost momentum, with weaker sentiment evident in both South Atlantic and West Africa. On C3, offers continued to edge lower, with discussions centring on around $33.00 for index dates versus bids remaining in the $32s, highlighting the widening gap between owners’ expectations and charterers’ willingness to pay.
PANAMAX
Activity in the Atlantic remained subdued today, with brokers reporting very limited fresh interest. The few trans-Atlantic bids that emerged were below previously concluded levels, contributing to what was described as a growing stand-off between Owners and Charterers. Market participants indicated that sentiment remains negative for both Atlantic and fronthaul business, despite vessel availability remaining relatively tight in the Western Mediterranean and the North Continent not appearing oversupplied. The P5TC declined by $94 on the day to settle at $17,896, reflecting the softer conditions seen in the Atlantic basin. Views on the Pacific market were more mixed. While some participants believe the market may have reached a floor, citing early signs of improving demand, others remain cautious. Supportive factors in the Pacific include increasing trading opportunities for Owners and a number of Charterers entering the market seeking replacement tonnage following weather-related disruptions. These developments have provided some near-term support to freight rates and may help stabilise sentiment should demand continue to improve.

Atlantic
The Eastern Heather (82,270 2022) open Bilbao 3 August was reported to have been placed on subjects for an Atlantic round, with some suggesting for a trip via Bolivar to Safi with Glencore at $21,000. The scrubber fitted Star Sky (81,466 2010) open prompt in Algeciras was said to have fixed for a US East Coast fronthaul at around $29,000-$30,000 to Western Bulk.

Pacific
The M Explorer (82,094 2010) open Chiba 31 July was said to have fixed a North Pacific round at $16,000, while the scrubber fitted Pedhoulas Rose (82,068 2017) open Shibushi also fixed a North Pacific round at $16,400 with the scrubber benefit for owners. The Kerkyra (81,375 2012) open Fangcheng 31 July/1 August was placed on subjects for a trip via Australia to China with grains at $14,250 to Norden. Messrs Daiichi were said to have fixed the scrubber fitted Venus History (95,700 2011) open Yosu end July for a trip via Villanueva with iron ore to Japan, although a rate did not materialise. The Great Amber (82,773 2023) open Tachibana 1 August was said to be on subjects, but no further details were heard.

SUPRAMAX
Another quiet day with the market yet to get going this week. The Index was negative across the board today with the 11TC average down another $269 to settle at $20,837. There were few rumoured or reported trades to reflect the negative sentiment, however the Ionic Spirit (56,108 2010) was rumoured to have fixed delivery North coast South America for a trip to Turkey with Aries Bulk at $24,000, whilst in Asia the Porto Kioni (56,025 2013) prompt Weihai was said to have fixed a trip to West Africa at around $14,000 for the first 75 days, but further details were lacking and a source also suggested this must have been for bulk cargo, as steels/generals were still paying much better levels with a Supramax apparently fixed at $19,000 on this route recently.
HANDYSIZE
The Handy market experienced a largely flat day, with regional sentiment continuing to be driven by positional factors and no clear catalyst emerging to shift the market direction. The BHSI closed at 900, while the 7TC average fell by $48 to settle at $16,207. Across the Continent and Mediterranean only minor changes were recorded and the market appeared broadly balanced, with rates assessed slightly below previous levels. The South Atlantic and US Gulf maintained a softer tone, as a lack of fresh demand combined with a further build-up in available tonnage continued to weigh on sentiment and keep rates under pressure. Meanwhile the Pacific market remained subdued, with limited fixing activity reported and little change in underlying fundamentals.

Market Fundamentals
India Tightens Grip on Iron Ore Grade Reporting

Odisha has intensified checks on iron ore grade assessments after allegations that some mining companies understated ore grades to lower royalty payments, Bloomberg News reported. The Directorate of Mines and Geology issued show-cause notices to 65 leaseholders, including Tata Steel, JSW Steel, SAIL, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel and Odisha Mining Corporation. Inspections found dispatched ore grades deviating from levels approved in mining plans. Tighter verification could squeeze near-term shipments and push up domestic ore costs, with Paradip accounting for around 40% of Indian seaborne iron ore exports, according to vessel tracking data. As of 22 July, Indian iron ore exports stood 7.7% higher on the year at 16.4 Mt, vessel tracking data show.

ai_analysis.summary: 2026年7月28日波罗的海干散货指数全线下挫，BDI跌32点至2664，各船型指数均呈跌势。Capesize受大西洋太平洋双重压力领跌，C3/C5航线价格回落；Panamax大西洋持续僵持，太平洋出现见底迹象；Supramax及Handysize活动清淡。FFA曲线显示近月合约承压，Cal27以后期限相对持稳。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: 干散货市场整体回调，各船型指数全线下跌。Capesize因油价回落及货主观望情绪加重领跌，Panamax大西洋僵持局面延续，太平洋受NOPAC及澳洲粮食需求支撑初现企稳迹象。船舶供给方面大西洋相对平衡，太平洋供应仍显充裕。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Capesize：C5西澳-青岛航线$12.17，跌0.455；C3巴西-青岛$33.78，跌0.58。Panamax：P5TC指数$17,896，跌94。Supramax：11TC指数$20,837，跌269。Handysize：7TC指数$16,207，跌48。各航线价格均呈下行趋势，市场情绪偏弱。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注Pacific Panamax能否守住$14-15k区间，NOPAC及澳洲粮食需求为关键支撑。Atlantic Capesize C3大西洋端货主与船东议价分歧扩大，$32-33区间争夺激烈。FFA近月合约Cape Aug26在32,350-32,500，Panamax Aug26在18,700-18,750，可关注套利机会。

market_watch: Capesize大西洋太平洋双弱，C3/C5航线价格持续承压，关注$12及$33关键支撑
Panamax大西洋僵持延续，Pacific端NOPAC及澳洲粮食需求能否持续改善为市场焦点
FFA曲线Cal27以后期限相对平稳，近月合约跌幅较大，期限结构值得关注

route_focus.view: 巴西-青岛航线价格$33.78，日跌$0.58。大西洋端情绪走弱，货主报价$32s vs船东要价$33，价差扩大显示市场偏向货主。巴西主要矿商仍有需求但压价意图明显，短期偏弱。
Skaw-Gibraltar大西洋往返航线$19,635，日跌$256。Atlantic端活动低迷，船东与货主陷入僵持。要价与还价差距拉大，指数日期船舶供给相对平衡，但需求不足抑制反弹空间。短期预计维持弱势整理。
Skaw-Passero至里约热内卢航线$8,618，日跌$18。Handysize市场整体平稳，大西洋与太平洋地区无明显方向性驱动。船舶供需基本平衡，费率变化幅度有限，预计短期维持现状。
